title: autocraft-econ-prescriptor: auto-generate tenant batch/cache/quant defaults
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes: Introduce Autocraft Econ Prescriptor: auto-generates tenant-safe batching, cache and quantization defaults based on sampled workload profiles. Includes CLI dry-run mode and safety gates; no customer-visible API change.
commits: seed: add prototype heuristics and config model
service: implement prescriptor HTTP/GRPC endpoints and dry-run path
cli: add 'autocraft prescribe --tenant' and CSV export
tests: add unit and integration fixtures for cold/warm traffic profiles
docs: prescriptor README, example configs and rollout guide
description:
Context: Customers and internal SRE runs showed recurring tenant cost regressions due to inconsistent batch and cache defaults + risky quantization rollouts. This PR introduces 'Autocraft Econ Prescriptor' — a service and CLI that auto-generates tenant-scoped default profiles for batching, KV/prefix cache, and quantization candidate tiers by analyzing sample traffic traces and tenant unit-economic constraints.
Motivation: reduce manual playbook work, prevent regressions during model/quant rollouts, and give platform engineers a safe dry-run path before applying defaults.
Scope:
- New standalone service (services/econ-prescriptor) exposing a primary /v1/prescribe endpoint and a dry-run mode; accepts sampled profile and tenant budget targets and returns candidate defaults.
- CLI integration (cli/autocraft) to run against local or remote prescriptor with CSV/JSON export.
- Migration helper script to export/import tenant defaults to the centralized defaults store (no automatic writes in this PR).
- Telemetry and gating: prescriptor emits selection_reason metrics and a safety_score; decisions require passing a minimal safety_score and an opt-in flag for automated apply.
Design notes:
- Prescriptor uses a two-stage pipeline: workload summarizer (sampled sequence length distributions, concurrency histogram, prefix-hit rates) then rule synthesizer (heuristics + unit-econ evaluator). The synthesizer prefers conservative presets for cold/warm traffic and proposes quant candidates annotated with expected latency delta and cost delta.
- Safety model: each candidate is scored against latency SLO impact (simulated using cached microbenchmarks) and unit cost delta; candidates below configured safety thresholds are flagged for manual review.
- Dry-run mode: CLI can run with --dry-run which returns the candidate set and a risk report but does not apply anything.
- Backward compatibility: the defaults store format was extended with a new optional "source" and "safety_score" fields; reads remain compatible.
Checklist:
- [x] Prototype heuristics and unit-econ library
- [x] Service + API + CLI dry-run
- [x] Integration tests for cold/warm traces
- [x] Telemetry metrics and dashboard skeleton
- [x] Docs and rollout guide
- [x] Migration script (manual apply only)
Security & compliance: service runs with tenant-scoped RBAC; migration script requires a service-account with defaults-write permission.
Tests & CI: Initial CI failed due to flaky prescriptor integration test (timing around microbenchmark mock). Fixed by adding deterministic mock responses and tighter assertions. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, lint, integration).
Review conversation summary:
- Marco Liu requested clearer telemetry labels and a compact metric for "prescriptor_decisions_total"; addressed in commit 3.
- Priya Desai asked to add one more e2e case simulating a heavy cold-start tenant; addressed by adding tests/e2e/prescriptor_integration.test.ts.
- Ethan Park asked to gate any automatic apply behavior behind a feature flag (SRE/ops opt-in); added config PRESCRIPTOR_AUTO_APPLY=false by default and documented rollout steps.
- Discussion about on-prem installer: added a note in docs/operations/prescriptor.md about packaging the prescriptor in the Private Installer.
Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature flag (PRESCRIPTOR_ENABLED=false).
2) Deploy to staging and exercise CLI dry-run on sampled tenants.
3) Open a small pilot with two internal tenants using manual apply.
4) After 2 weeks of stable telemetry and no negative-regressions, consider enabling automated-apply opt-in for a limited tenant cohort.
Migration notes: the migrate-defaults script generates a CSV of candidate defaults and a JSON risk-report; manual review required. No destructive migration performed in this PR.
Related items: ENG-5781 (unit-econ evaluator), ENG-5790 (prescriptor telemetry), SUP-1123 (customer report referencing noisy quant rollouts).
Merge outcome: squash-merged into main on 2026-02-15.
Follow-ups (tracked in Linear):
- Add model-driven quant simulation harness (ENG-5840)
- Add user-facing Console control to preview prescriptor recommendations (DES-901)
